title: Tomato and basil sauce
intro: About 600 g of simple, sweet sauce: dresses 4 servings of pasta or serves as a base.

steps.t: Pass the tomatoes through a food mill, or crush them with a fork if you like it chunky.
In a saucepan, warm the oil with the crushed garlic over low heat for 2 minutes, until just golden.
steps.label: Garlic

steps.t: Pour in the tomatoes, add the salt and bring to a boil.
Simmer partly covered over medium-low heat for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and the oil rises.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Remove the garlic, turn off the heat and add the basil torn by hand and a drizzle of fresh olive oil.

tips.t: Use half a chopped onion instead of garlic for a sweeter sauce that kids love.
It freezes perfectly in single-portion jars for 3 months.

title: Bolognese ragù
intro: Slow-cooked with milk and little tomato: the tender ragù for tagliatelle and lasagna.

steps.t: Finely chop the carrot, celery and onion; cut the pancetta into very small cubes.
In a heavy pan, brown the pancetta in the oil for 3 minutes, then add the vegetables and cook gently for 8 minutes.
steps.label: Soffritto

steps.t: Raise the heat, add the beef and break it up with a spoon: brown it for 10 minutes, until the liquid is gone and it sizzles.
steps.label: Beef

steps.t: Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 3 minutes, until you no longer smell alcohol.
steps.label: Wine

steps.t: Add the passata and the tomato paste dissolved in a ladle of broth, then season with salt and pepper.
Cover loosely and cook on the lowest heat for 2 hours 40 minutes, adding broth if it dries: it should just simmer.
steps.label: Ragù

pressure.t: Close the pressure cooker and, once it hisses, cook for 40 minutes on low heat; release the pressure and open.

steps.t: Add the milk a little at a time and cook 20 more minutes, until absorbed and the ragù is tender.
steps.label: Milk

steps.t: Taste and adjust the salt. It's even better after a night in the fridge.

tips.t: In Bologna it goes with egg tagliatelle, never spaghetti.
Layer it with pasta sheets and béchamel for classic lasagna alla bolognese.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge and 3 months in the freezer, in portions.

title: Pesto Genovese
intro: Basil pounded in a mortar with pine nuts, garlic and cheese: bright green and fragrant.

steps.t: Wash the basil in cold water and pat it dry with a towel, without rubbing the leaves.
In a mortar, pound the garlic with a few grains of coarse salt to a paste.
Add the basil a little at a time and grind it in circles against the sides, until it releases a bright green liquid.
Add the pine nuts and grind everything to a cream.
Stir in the grated cheeses, then drizzle in the oil, mixing with the pestle.
Use it right away and never heat it: to dress pasta, loosen it with a spoonful of the cooking water.

tips.t: Classic with trofie or trenette, cooked together with diced potatoes and green beans.
Using a blender? Chill the jar in the freezer first and pulse: the basil won't darken.
Under a film of oil it stays green for 3 days in the fridge; freeze it without the cheese.

title: Puttanesca sauce
intro: Neapolitan-style olives, capers and tomato: a bold sauce ready in half an hour.

steps.t: Rinse the capers and leave them in a bowl of cold water for 10 minutes to remove the salt.
steps.label: Capers

steps.t: Meanwhile, pit and halve the olives, and chop the parsley.
In a wide pan, fry the garlic and chili in the oil over medium heat for 1-2 minutes, without browning them.
steps.label: Garlic

steps.t: Add the olives and drained capers, stir for 1 minute, then pour in the tomatoes crushed by hand.
Cook over high heat for 15 minutes, stirring, until the sauce reduces and turns glossy.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Turn off the heat and finish with oregano and parsley. Taste before salting: olives and capers are already salty.

tips.t: Toss with spaghetti or vermicelli in the pan, and skip the cheese.
The Roman version melts 3-4 anchovy fillets into the oil with the garlic.

title: Lentil ragù
intro: Lentils, soffritto and tomato cooked slowly: a rich, hearty plant-based ragù.

steps.t: Rinse the lentils in a sieve. Finely chop the carrot, celery and onion.
Cook the chopped vegetables gently in the oil for 8 minutes, until soft and golden.
steps.label: Soffritto

steps.t: Add the tomato paste and toast it for 1 minute, stir in the lentils and deglaze with the wine for 2 minutes.
steps.label: Wine

steps.t: Pour in the passata and broth, add the rosemary and bay leaf and bring to a boil.

pressure.t: Pour in the passata and only 350 ml of broth, add the rosemary and bay leaf and close the pressure cooker.

steps.t: Cover and cook on low heat for 35 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are tender and the sauce thick.
steps.label: Ragù

pressure.t: Once it hisses, cook for 12 minutes on low heat, then let the pressure drop naturally.

steps.t: Remove the herbs and season. For a creamier ragù, blend a ladleful and stir it back in.

tips.t: Great with rigatoni or mezze maniche and, if it needn't be vegan, grated pecorino.
Layer it with béchamel and pasta sheets for a vegetarian lasagna everyone loves.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well in portions.

title: Amatriciana sauce
intro: Crispy guanciale, tomato and pecorino: Amatrice's sauce for bucatini and spaghetti.

steps.t: Cut the rind off the guanciale and slice it into strips 1 cm thick.
Brown it in an iron pan without oil over medium heat for 7 minutes, until the fat is translucent and the edges crisp.
steps.label: Guanciale

steps.t: Pour in the wine and let it evaporate for 1 minute.
steps.label: Wine

steps.t: Set half the guanciale aside to keep it crisp. Add the crumbled chili and the crushed tomatoes.
Cook for 15 minutes over medium heat until thick. Taste before salting: guanciale and pecorino are salty.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Return the reserved guanciale. Toss the pasta in the sauce off the heat and finish with pecorino.

tips.t: Serve with al dente bucatini or spaghetti, tossed in the sauce with a splash of pasta water.
Add the pecorino off the heat: if the sauce is boiling, the cheese turns lumpy.
